questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I went to Berlin on exchange, first and foremost as I've always wanted to try to live in the city. Furthermore, I wanted to improve my German, why it was a good opportunity.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite hard to find information regarding the courses taught at the university and additionally, to understand how to apply for courses. I had to a lot of research myself to be able to understand the system.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was a part of a Buddy-program, where I was partnered with a person studying the same major at the university. Furthermore, the university arranged information meetings.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found an apartment in Berlin through a service called Wunderflats, which was great and worked without any problems. However, it was quite expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Many students lived on campus, why a big part of the social life was at the campus site.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration for courses was really difficult and not designed for international students. Few courses were provided in English and both the registration for courses, the acceptance and the registration for exams had to be done on platforms in German and by email to the professors.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I contacted the professors a lot on email and they provided me with some necessary information, however they did not always have the answer needed as an exchange student. Furthermore, it was possible to contact the international office at the university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got accepted to all of my courses after writing emails to the professors.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Engage with a student who attends the university, who is able to help you obtain the necessary information as it can be quite hard to figure the system out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had three courses at bachelor level and one at master level. Some of the courses were well-structured and informative, however some did not live up to the expected level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The courses I was signed up to only did class-teaching once a week. Therefore, I did not have any seminars.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Introduction to family sociology
- Policy-making in the European policy cycle
- Judicialization of politics from a comparative perspective
- International Institutions

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Except for my course Judicialization, the courses were well-structured and the professors were helpful and competent.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and transport are very cheap compared to Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It was possible to attend various clubs and sports, however due to COVID, a lot of the activities were shut down.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I participated in some activities arranged by the international office in order to meet other exchange students, which is recommendable.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit the different parts of the city and walk around.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Except for understanding the educational system and the structure of the university, it was easy to adjust.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Due to COVID, it was difficult to meet the local students as a lot of my classes were only taught online.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The relationship between professor and student is a lot more formal and the German students were much more polite than what I am used to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The way the people engage with each other more openly and polite.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to do a lot of paperwork, contact your professors early on and attend the information meetings.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It loved living in Berlin.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to figure the structure of the educational system out on my own and having to fill out a lot of paperwork.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
